optimizedDescription.value: Detect VCS, content, derivation, schema, and coverage staleness; warn-not-block reads; lock index; latch monotonic freshness.

optimizedContext.value:
# Staleness Detection

## Rules

- Indexer accepts optional `vcsRef: string` in `IndexOptions`. After successful index, persist opaque ref in graph-store metadata key `lastIndexedRef` (git hash, hg changeset, or any `VcsAdapter.ref()` string). Omit `vcsRef` -> `lastIndexedRef` stays `null` (staleness unavailable; valid).
- Stale: `lastIndexedRef !== null` AND query-time `VcsAdapter.ref()` differs. Fresh: non-null and equal. `lastIndexedRef === null` -> unknown. Unknown SHALL NOT be treated as stale.
- Derivation mismatch is distinct from VCS freshness. Fingerprint from: effective `@specd/code-graph` package version loaded by running CLI; canonical hash of resolved workspace objects from active `specd.yaml`; effective discovery configuration used by indexer; newline-normalized content hashes of resolution manifests declared by registered language adapters.
- CRLF vs LF of an unchanged resolution manifest MUST NOT mismatch by itself. Normalized manifest text differing from index-time hash SHALL mismatch derivation even if VCS ref unchanged; VCS freshness stays fresh.
- Warn-not-block: read commands (`graph stats`, `graph search`, `graph impact`, `graph hotspots`) warn when stale and always return current (possibly stale) results. No block.
- Reads SHALL surface derivation-mismatch metadata and SHALL NOT treat a mismatched graph as fresh. `graph index` repairs: recreate active graph and full rebuild with visible reason, OR fail requiring force re-index (different code-graph version or workspace configuration). Independent of VCS freshness; graph MAY be VCS-fresh and still need rebuild.
- `GraphStatistics` includes `lastIndexedRef: string | null` beside `lastIndexedAt`. No stored ref -> `null`.
- Text: after `Last indexed`, when stale append `⚠ Graph is stale (indexed at <7-char-ref>, current: <7-char-ref>)`. `lastIndexedRef === null`: no staleness line. Derivation mismatch append `⚠ Derivation fingerprint mismatch — code-graph version, workspace configuration, or resolution manifest content changed`.
- JSON/TOON: `stale` `boolean | null` (`true` stale, `false` fresh, `null` unknown); `currentRef` `string | null`; `fingerprintMismatch` `boolean | null` (`true` differs, `false` matches, `null` no stored fingerprint).
- `@specd/code-graph` (or providers) owns filesystem index lock: acquire, release, `assertGraphIndexUnlocked`. Path inside config dir (`.specd/config/graph/index.lock`). CLI, MCP, other clients assert lock to prevent concurrent indexing.
- Primitives `isGraphStale` and fingerprint helpers stay here. Hosts MUST NOT reimplement VCS ref resolution plus staleness and fingerprint assembly inline when `GetGraphHealth` is available. `GetGraphHealth` (`code-graph:get-graph-health`) is canonical orchestration for `graph stats`, `project status --graph`, and SDK snapshot builders.
- `@specd/code-graph` merges workspace `allowedPaths`, `excludePaths`, `respectGitignore` plus global params and runtime/CLI overrides (`--include-path`, `--exclude-path`) into effective `ProjectGraphConfig`.
- No discovered `specd.yaml`: synthetic fallback `SpecdConfig` maps repository root to one synthetic `default` workspace so index, stats, search can run.
- Canonical health distinguishes VCS-ref freshness, working-tree/content freshness, derivation fingerprint compatibility, backend schema/generation compatibility, and index coverage completeness. Matching VCS ref MUST NOT imply fresh content when tracked or untracked working-tree files differ from indexed content.
- Health exposes stable machine-readable reasons: dirty, unknown, partial, excluded, unsupported, parse-failed, fingerprint-mismatched, schema-incompatible. Consumers MAY call a missing symbol stale only when the addressed target has current content and complete supported coverage. Every other absence is inconclusive.
- Installed `@specd/code-graph` version participates in project and workspace derivation fingerprints. A release with the enriched reference model MUST change that version. Backend schema versions stay separate from package derivation and from `schema-std`.
- Every workspace and the aggregate graph persist `knownStaleSinceLastIndex`. True aggregate latch returns immediately without rescanning inputs. First proven stale workspace or project-global input atomically sets the affected workspace latch when applicable and the aggregate latch. Only a successful index clears latches.
- Freshness state: `current`, `stale`, or `unknown`. Aggregate precedence `stale > unknown > current`. Read, stat, hash, repository, or VCS failures return transient `unknown`, MUST NOT set stale flags or latches, and SHALL be retried later.
- Batch `AssessIndexedResourceFreshness` assesses exact files, documents, and specs from persisted indexed-input observations. Matching filesystem mtime and size SHALL avoid content reads. Changed stamps trigger hashing; equal content refreshes observations; different or missing content monotonically marks the input stale. Repository inputs use stable revision or fingerprint.
- Resource stale when any input is stale; unknown when none is stale but at least one cannot be assessed. Exact resource consumers MAY use current targeted evidence despite unrelated global staleness. Corpus-wide absence, uniqueness, ranking, or workspace fallback MUST keep global stale/unknown diagnostics; validating returned resources cannot prove completeness.
- VCS-backed workspaces sharing one repository root share one diff evaluation and keep independent workspace latches. Scope identity derives from sorted workspace names and MUST NOT persist or hash absolute paths. Normalized fingerprint sorts graph-visible `{ path, state, contentHash }` entries and distinguishes present vs missing paths.
- Filter `VcsAdapter.modifiedFiles()` through the same effective `excludePaths`, `allowedPaths`, gitignore, default exclusion, and explicit code/document/spec channels used by indexing before stat or hashing. Additions, modifications, deletions, or either rename side excluded from every applicable channel MUST NOT affect workspace or graph health. Mixed diffs include only visible paths. Effective visibility configuration changes invalidate the derivation fingerprint.
- Non-VCS workspaces compare visible membership and persisted observations, stopping at the first proven mismatch. Workspaces with `respectGitignore: false` under VCS use hybrid VCS and filesystem assessment for ignored untracked graph inputs.

## Constraints

- VCS-agnostic via `VcsAdapter` from `@specd/core`.
- VCS ref stored as opaque string.
- Detecting staleness never triggers re-indexing.
- Lock files, bootstrap configs, config merging, and staleness calculations live in `@specd/code-graph` (or `@specd/core`), not CLI helpers.
